body:
MEASURED on the operator's own device and deployed server, 2026-08-18.

The Kobo uploads a DELTA, never its full set. So any annotation created while
CWNG was not capturing is invisible to the server forever — the device will not
re-offer it, and `checkforchanges` containment (correctly) keeps the book out of
the Kobo-cloud download.

Measured gap, same user, same 4 books, device vs server:

  | book                | device highlights | server annotations |
  |---------------------|-------------------|--------------------|
  | The Able McLaughlins| 1                 | 1                  |
  | 1984                | 10                | 2                  |
  | Alice Adams         | 2                 | 0                  |
  | The Age of Innocence| 4                 | 4                  |

10 device-only highlights. I did NOT establish why each was missed — the missing
ones cluster in windows where the device was being driven for instrumentation,
so pointing the device at a capture proxy is at least as likely an explanation
as a live defect. What is established:

- the LIVE path is healthy. A highlight created on hardware just now
  ("surveillance", 1984) reached the server within seconds with correct text,
  type and source. So this is not an active sync bug.
- there is NO automatic recovery. `kobo_annotation_seed_capture` and
  `kobo_annotation_seed_capture_page` are both EMPTY on the deployed server, and
  `kobo_device_book_annotation_state` and `annotation_device_state` likewise. The
  seeding machinery exists in the schema and has never run.
- the designed manual recovery — uploading KoboReader.sqlite via
  `/annotations/import` — silently drops dogears and note-only rows, and cannot
  apply an edit to an annotation the server already has. Both recorded
  separately.

So the product's answer to "the server missed one" is currently: nothing
automatic, and a manual path with known holes. That is the gap worth closing, and
it is independent of whichever cause produced these particular 10.
title: Annotations made outside a working capture window are unrecoverable, and no seed capture has ever run
